sources.entry: LanguageTool - Proofread more than 20 languages. It finds many errors that a simple spell checker cannot detect. (Source Code, Clients) LGPL-2.1 Java/Docker

summary.one_liner: LanguageTool is open-source multilingual proofreading software that checks grammar and style in more than 20 languages and catches errors a plain spell checker misses.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes LanguageTool as proofreading software for English, Spanish, French, German, Portuguese, Polish, Dutch and more than 20 other languages. It finds errors that a simple spell checker cannot detect. The README links to a forum, instructions for running your own LanguageTool server, HTTP API documentation, instructions for using the public server over HTTP, and Javadoc for using it from Java. It includes a scripted install.sh that can install, build, or remove LanguageTool and offers GUI, command-line, and server run modes. It can also build standalone, Wikipedia, and LibreOffice/OpenOffice extension packages from source. Community-maintained Docker images are listed by name, and contributors can add error detection rules.
use_cases: add a grammar checker to LibreOffice or OpenOffice
how_to_run: sudo bash install.sh (via the curl one-liner in the README)
Run the GUI, commandline, or server command from the installer
notable: Covers more than 20 languages with rule-based error detection beyond spell checking
Installer script supports GUI, command-line and server modes
Can build LibreOffice/OpenOffice extension and Wikipedia packages
Public HTTP API and option to run a private server
caveats: Full clone needs more than 500 MiB to download and over 1,500 MiB on disk; a shallow clone is smaller
Building from source requires Java 17 and Maven
Mac M1/M2 users need to run builds under Rosetta with x86_64 Homebrew
